perspective:
**Christian Mensah’s available information:**

- He is a police officer and has been close friends with Jonathan since childhood. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and knows Jonathan is more educated/has a master’s degree. They have a favorite coffee shop.
- Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important from him, which made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged and attended a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront Jonathan.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt something was wrong and that Jonathan had been acting differently. He heard Jonathan admit he was hiding something, that Jonathan was in trouble, and that Jonathan hadn’t known how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help, said they could face it together, and asked what Jonathan needed. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian in, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that Jonathan did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to investigate discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up. He felt determined and protective, decided to clear Jonathan’s name, and began gathering evidence.
- Christian told Jonathan he believed Jonathan was being framed and that he had leads, though he was not yet sure who was responsible. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later came to believe the culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it—someone they both know and trust—and planned to confront them and bring them to justice.
- Jonathan warned Christian that the person is dangerous and told Christian he trusts him. The specific identity of the culprit is not disclosed in the provided dialogue.
